Rashi on Meilah 2b:10:1.hebrew: ואכתי מאי קמ"ל דעולא אי משום דמתו נמי תנינא - דאין מועלין בהן, דתנן לקמן בפ' הנהנה ש"פ מן ההקדש (מעילה דף יח.):
Rashi on Meilah 2b:10:1.english: And still, what is Ulla teaching us? If it is because [of animals that] died — we also learned [this] - that one does not commit me'ilah with them [by Torah law], as we learned later in the chapter [beginning] "One who derives benefit [worth a perutah] from Hekdesh" (Meilah 18a).

Rashi on Meilah 2b:10:2.english: One who derives benefit from the sin offering - [that is,] one that has a blemish.

Rashi on Meilah 2b:10:3.hebrew: כשהיא חיה לא מעל עד שיפגום - עד שיחסר ממנו. דכיון דקדושת דמים היא, לא מעל עד שיחסר מדמיה, כגון שתלש מן הצמר או שחרש בה והכחישה, דכיון דבעלת מום היא, קיימא לדמיה. וקי"ל: כל העומד לדמים — אין מועלין בו עד שיחסר מדמיו. אבל כל שאינו עומד לדמים, כגון כוס של זהב של הקדש, כיון (שנהנה ממנו) שנהנה בו, אע"פ שלא חיסרו — מעל. וכשהיא מתה, דלאו לדמי קיימא, דאין פודין את הקדשים להאכילן לכלבים, כיון שנהנה בשוה פרוטה — מעל, אף על פי שלא חיסרו. והאי מעל מדרבנן הוא, דלאחר שמתה ד"ה אין בה מעילה מדאורייתא. אלא מאי מעל? מדרבנן. והכא הוא בחטאת מתה דמעל, דחמורה קדושתה דלכפרה אתיא. אבל בשאר קדשים, כגון עולה ואשם ושלמי צבור, משום דלאו לכפרה אתו, כיון שמתו לית בהו מעילה אפילו מדרבנן, וקשה לעולא. אמר לך עולא: ה"ה דבכל קדשי קדשים ס"ל לתנא נמי דמעל. ומ"ש דנקט בחטאת טפי משאר קדשי קדשים? דסד"א הואיל ולכפרה אתיא, דכשהיא חיה קיימא לחטאת:
Rashi on Meilah 2b:10:3.english: When it is alive, he is not liable for misuse until he damages it - Until something is diminished from it. For since it has the sanctity of monetary value, he is not liable for misuse until its value is diminished, for example, if he plucked some of the wool, or plowed with it and weakened it; for since it is blemished, it stands for its value. And we hold: anything that stands for its monetary value, one is not liable for misuse of it until its value is diminished. But anything that does not stand for its monetary value, such as a golden cup of the Temple property, since he derived benefit from it, even though he did not diminish it, he is liable for misuse. And when it is dead, since it does not stand for its value (for one does not redeem consecrated items to feed them to dogs), once he derives benefit worth a *peruta*, he is liable for misuse, even though he did not diminish it. And this misuse is rabbinic, for after it died, everyone agrees that there is no misuse by Torah law. Rather, what [kind of] misuse is it? Rabbinic. And here it is with a dead sin offering that [the Mishnah says] there is misuse, since its sanctity is more stringent, as it comes for atonement. But with other offerings, such as a burnt offering, a guilt offering, and communal peace offerings, because they do not come for atonement, once they have died there is no misuse in them even by rabbinic law — and this is difficult for Ulla. Ulla could say to you: The same applies to all most-holy offerings, that the Tanna also holds there is misuse. And why did [the Tanna] mention a sin offering rather than other most-holy offerings? Because one might have thought: since it comes for atonement, [it would be treated differently, in that] while it is alive it stands [to be used] for a sin offering.

Rashi on Meilah 2b:1:1.english: A dilemma was raised before them - Regarding these [offerings] that were taught in the Mishnah, in which one deviated [from the proper procedure], for example, where one slaughtered [them] in the south, or received their blood in the south, etc.:

Rashi on Meilah 2b:1:2.hebrew: אם עלו למזבח מהו שירדו - צריך להורידן או לא:
Rashi on Meilah 2b:1:2.english: If they ascended the altar, what is [the law] that they descend - Must one bring them down, or not?

Rashi on Meilah 2b:2:1.hebrew: אליבא דר' יהודה - דאמר התם בפרק המזבח מקדש (זבחים דף פד.): ״זאת היא העולה״, הרי אלו מיעוטים — פרט לשנשפך דמה, ושלנה, ושיצאה (וניתנין למעלה שנתנן למטה או הניתנין למטה שנתנן למעלה), שאם עלו — ירדו. כולי עלמא לא פליגי דהני נמי אם עלו ירדו:
Rashi on Meilah 2b:2:1.english: According to Rabbi Yehuda - For he says there, in the chapter [entitled] "Hamizbe'ach Mekadesh" (Zevachim 84a): "This is the burnt offering" — behold, these are limitations — excluding [an offering] whose blood was spilled, and [one] that was left overnight, and [one] that went out [of the courtyard] (and [offerings] that are to be placed above that were placed below, or that are to be placed below that were placed above), [teaching] that if they ascended [the altar], they must descend. Everyone agrees that these too, if they ascended, must descend:

Rashi on Meilah 2b:2:2.hebrew: כי פליגי אליבא דר"ש - דפליג עליה דרבי יהודה, ואמר: ״זאת תורת העולה״ — ריבה תורה אחת לכל העולים, שאם עלו לא ירדו:
Rashi on Meilah 2b:2:2.english: They disagree according to Rabbi Shimon - Who disagrees with Rabbi Yehuda and says: "This is the law of the burnt offering" (Leviticus 6:2) — [the verse] included one law for all [disqualified] burnt offerings, that if they ascended [the altar], they do not descend.

Rashi on Meilah 2b:3:1.hebrew: רב יוסף כר"ש - דכי היכי דאמר ר"ש הניתנין למטה שנתנן למעלה וכו', דהיינו שינוי מקום מתן דמים, שאם עלו לא ירדו, ה"ה נמי היכא דשני במקום שחיטה, ששחטן בדרום, שאם עלו לא ירדו:
Rashi on Meilah 2b:3:1.english: Rav Yosef [holds] like Rabbi Shimon - For just as Rabbi Shimon said, "Those [blood-applications] that are to be placed below that were placed above," etc. — that is, a change in the place of the application of the blood — that if they went up [on the altar] they do not come down, so too, the same applies where one changed the place of slaughter, [such as] where one slaughtered them in the south, that if they went up they do not come down.

Rashi on Meilah 2b:3:2.hebrew: רבה אמר לך עד כאן לא קאמר ר"ש - התם: אם עלו, לא ירדו:
Rashi on Meilah 2b:3:2.english: Rabba could have said to you: Rabbi Shimon only stated - there [in the mishna's case], that if they ascended [the altar], they shall not descend.

Rashi on Meilah 2b:3:3.hebrew: אלא בניתנין למטה וכו' - כלומר, דלא אמר רבי שמעון דלא ירדו, אלא באותו שינוי מקום דמתן דמים, הואיל ושחיטה וקבלה הוי בצפון:
Rashi on Meilah 2b:3:3.english: Only with regard to those placed below, etc. - That is, [Rabbi Shimon] did not say that they do not descend except in the case of that change of place in the placing of the blood, since the slaughter and the receiving [of the blood] took place in the north.

Rashi on Meilah 2b:4:1.hebrew: אבל הכא וכו' - ואם עלו, ירדו:
Rashi on Meilah 2b:4:1.english: But here, etc. - And if they went up [on the altar], they must come down.

Rashi on Meilah 2b:5:1.hebrew: בשלמא לרב יוסף - דאמר אם עלו לא ירדו, הואיל ולא ירדו מקדושתן, מש"ה מועלין בהן:
Rashi on Meilah 2b:5:1.english: Granted, according to Rav Yosef - who said that if they ascended [the altar] they do not descend; since they did not descend from their sanctity, therefore one is liable for misusing them.

Rashi on Meilah 2b:5:2.hebrew: אלא לרבה - דאמר דאם עלו ירדו, דיצאו מקדושתן, קשיא: דאמאי מועלין בהן?
Rashi on Meilah 2b:5:2.english: But according to Rabba - who said that if they ascended [the altar] they must descend, because they have left their sanctity, it is difficult: For why is one liable for misusing them?

Rashi on Meilah 2b:5:3.hebrew: מאי מועלין מדרבנן - אבל מדאורייתא לית בהו קדושה, ואם עלו — ירדו:
Rashi on Meilah 2b:5:3.english: What [is the meaning of] "one is liable for misusing them"? [It is] by rabbinic law - But by Torah law, there is no sanctity in them, and if they went up [onto the altar], they must come down.

Rashi on Meilah 2b:7:1.hebrew: מעילה דרבנן - משלם קרן ולא חומש, משום דחומש מפני איל אשם מייתי ליה, ובדרבנן ליכא קרבן, דהוי כמביא חולין לעזרה. הילכך לא מייתי נמי חומש. אבל במעילה דאורייתא מייתי קרן וחומש ואשם מעילה:
Rashi on Meilah 2b:7:1.english: Misuse by rabbinic law - He pays the principal but not the added fifth, because the fifth is brought on account of the guilt-offering ram, and in a rabbinic [case] there is no offering, since it would be like bringing non-sacred [animals] into the Temple courtyard. Therefore he also does not bring the fifth. But in misuse by Torah law, he brings the principal, the fifth, and the guilt-offering for misuse.

Rashi on Meilah 2b:7:2.hebrew: דבר תורה - מדקאמר דבר תורה, אלמא מדאורייתא לית בהו מעילה, אלא מדרבנן. ה"נ לרבה, מאי דקאמר מועלין — מדרבנן:
Rashi on Meilah 2b:7:2.english: By Torah law - Since [Rabbi Yochanan] said "by Torah law," evidently by Torah law there is no misuse in them, but [there is] by rabbinic law. So too according to Rabba, what [he means by] "they are subject to misuse" is by rabbinic law:

Rashi on Meilah 2b:8:1.hebrew: לימא לרבה תנינא להא דעולא א"ר יוחנן - דממתניתין נמי שמעינן לה. מי לא אמרינן דקדשי קדשים ששחטן בדרום כמאן דחנקינון דמו, והוו כקדשים שמתו, וקתני "מועלין בהן", ואמרינן מאי "מועלין" — מדרבנן, דמדאורייתא לית בהו מעילה, דקאמרינן "אם עלו ירדו", דכקדשים שמתו דמו? אם כן, היינו דעולא, ומאי קמ"ל הא דעולא:
Rashi on Meilah 2b:8:1.english: Let us say, according to Rabba, we learned that which Ulla said Rabbi Yochanan said - For we also hear it from the mishna. Did we not say that most-holy offerings slaughtered in the south are considered as if they had been strangled, and are like sacrifices that died, and [the mishna] teaches "one is liable for misuse of them," and we said: What is "one is liable for misuse"? [It means] by rabbinic law, for by Torah law there is no misuse in them, as we say, "If they went up [on the altar], they come down," because they are considered like sacrifices that died? If so, this is the same as [the statement] of Ulla, so what is [Ulla] teaching us with this statement of Ulla?

Rashi on Meilah 2b:8:2.english: And [the Gemara] answers: Even though we learned - it in the mishnah.

Rashi on Meilah 2b:8:3.hebrew: אצטריך הא דעולא דסד"א הכא - במתניתין, דקדשי קדשים ששחטן בדרום, לא בדילי אינשי מינייהו, משום דאע"ג ששינה בהן, מ"מ בכשרות נשחטו, ולא בדילי מינייהו אינשי. להכי מועלין בהן — אי לרב יוסף מדאורייתא, אי לרבה מדרבנן:
Rashi on Meilah 2b:8:3.english: The statement of Ulla was necessary, for it might have entered [your] mind [to say] that here - in our mishna, [concerning] the most sacred offerings that one slaughtered in the south, people do not distance themselves from them, because even though he changed [the place] with them, nevertheless they were slaughtered in the manner of valid offerings, and people do not distance themselves from them. Therefore, one is liable for misuse with them — according to Rav Yosef, by Torah law; according to Rabba, by rabbinic law.

Rashi on Meilah 2b:9:1.hebrew: אבל קדשים שמתו - דנבלות נינהו ומאיסי, ובדילי מינייהו אינשי. אימא: אפילו מדרבנן לית בהו מעילה, דהא בדילי מינייהו:
Rashi on Meilah 2b:9:1.english: But sacrificial animals that died - For they are carrion and are repulsive, and people distance themselves from them. One might say: even by rabbinic law there is no misuse [of consecrated property] in them, since people distance themselves from them.

Rashi on Meilah 2b:9:2.hebrew: קמ"ל - יצאו מידי מעילה דבר תורה, אבל מדרבנן אית בהו מעילה בקדשים שמתו:
Rashi on Meilah 2b:9:2.english: It teaches us - They have left the status of misuse [by] Torah law, but by rabbinic law there is misuse with regard to sacrificial animals that died.

Tosafot on Meilah 2b:1:1.hebrew: עלו מהו שירדו - ע"כ קאי אדרום; דאחוץ לזמנו וחוץ למקומו לא קאי, דהא משמע פרק המזבח מקדש (זבחים דף פד.) דלכ"ע לא ירדו; וגם לא קאי אלילה, דפלוגתא היא בהדיא בין רבי יהודה ור' שמעון:
Tosafot on Meilah 2b:1:1.english: "If they ascended, what is the law that they descend?" - Necessarily, it refers to [a case of slaughter in] the south; [for] it does not refer to [a case of slaughter] outside its time or outside its place, since it is implied in the chapter Hamizbe'ach Mekadesh (Zevachim 84a) that according to all opinions they do not descend; and it also does not refer to [a case of slaughter at] night, for it is an explicit dispute between Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon:

Tosafot on Meilah 2b:2:1.hebrew: אליבא דר' יהודה כולי עלמא לא פליגי דאם עלו ירדו - דהשתא גבי נשחט בלילה, דלא שחט בדרום, קאמר ירדו — כל שכן היכא דשחט בדרום, דשינה מקומו, דירדו. כי פליגי אליבא דר"ש דאמר גבי נשחט בלילה לא תרד: רב יוסף כר"ש (דאסר), דמדמה שינוי מקום לשינוי זמנו:
Tosafot on Meilah 2b:2:1.english: According to Rabbi Yehuda, everyone agrees that if they ascended, they must descend - For now, regarding [an offering] slaughtered at night, where [the slaughterer] did not slaughter in the south, he says that they must descend — all the more so where he slaughtered in the south, [in which case] he changed its place, that they must descend. They disagree [only] according to Rabbi Shimon, who said regarding [an offering] slaughtered at night that it does not descend: Rav Yosef [rules] like Rabbi Shimon (who prohibits), for he likens a change of place to a change of time:

Tosafot on Meilah 2b:3:1.hebrew: ורבה אמר לך עד כאן לא קאמר ר"ש אלא בניתנין למעלה שנתנן למטה כו' - תימה: אמאי שבק בלילה ונשפך דמה ויצאה דמה, דפליגי בהו רבי יהודה ור"ש, ונקט ניתנין למעלה שנתנן למטה, דאף רבי יהודה מודה דלא ירדו? ופירש הר"י דמיירי הכא בעוף, שעולתו למעלה ועשאה למטה, והכא לא מודה רבי יהודה משום דהוי כפסול; הילכך ירדו. דלא דמי ניתנין למעלה שנתנן למטה, דקאמר בזבחים (דף פד.) דלא פליג רבי יהודה, דהתם מיירי בבהמה שהיתה לה הכשר בשחיטה ובקבלה; אבל בעולת העוף שמלקה למטה, דלא היה שום הכשר, פליג רי יהודה כמו בנשחט בלילה ונשפך דמה. ועל זה מחלק רבה: דע"כ לא קאמר ר"ש לא ירדו (גבי זבחים) אלא משום דלא שינה בהן אלא במזבח עצמו, ולעולם זביחתן וקבלתן בצפון, כלומר כל מצותה וכל ענייניה. אבל בשחט בדרום מודה ר"ש דכמאן דחנקיה דמי, והוי כמו שחוטי חוץ, כיון שמשנה מקום שחיטה; ובשוחט חוץ לכ"ע אם עלו ירדו. מיהו קשה למורי רבינו ה"ר פרץ מהא דמותיב רב יוסף לקמן לרבה חדא מגו חדא כו', פי' דחזינן גבי מליקה דכששינה בה אם עלה לא ירד, וה"ה גבי שינוי בבהמה, ואיתותב רבה. ולפירוש ר"י אמאי איתותב משינוי מקום דמליקה? והא איהו מחלק הכא שפיר בין שינוי דעוף לגוף המזבח דבהמה מצפון לדרום! לכן נ"ל כדמשמע בפשוט דמיירי בבהמה, ואע"ג דמודה ביה ר' יהודה, מכל מקום מייתי לה לדומיא לשינוי מקום דהוי כי שינוי דדרום, ולסימנא בעלמא נקט; וכל זה דוחק. לכן נראה למורי רבינו ה"ר פרץ דהוצרך רבה להביא הא מילתא דניתנין למעלה שנתנן למטה, דאי לא אייתי אלא נשחטה בלילה, בהא ודאי איכא לפלוגי שפיר, דהתם שינוי זמן והכא שינוי מקום, ולא דמו כלל אהדדי. ועדיין היה קשה לו לרבה מניתנין למעלה שנתנן למטה. וכ"ת: מה ענין שינוי זריקה לשינוי שחיטה דגבי דרום? דהא בהא דניתנין למעלה שנתנן למטה אף ר"י מודה, משום דהוי פסול בזריקה, אבל הכא גבי דרום הוי פסול בשחיטה. הא לאו מילתא, דלר"ש מהני פסול בשחיטה כמו בזריקה לר' יהודה, דהא בנשחט בלילה דא"ר יהודה ירדו קאמר ר"ש לא ירדו, וא"כ מהשתא יש לנו לדמות שחט בדרום לר"ש לניתנין למעלה שנתנן למטה, וא"כ תיקשי לרבה. לכך הוצרך לחלק בין ניתנין למעלה לניתנין למטה בין שחט בדרום; אבל בין נשחט בלילה לשחט בדרום לא הוצרך לחלק, דאותו חילוק פשוט הוא וידוע לכל, דהתם שינוי זמן והכא שינוי מקום:
Tosafot on Meilah 2b:3:1.english: "And Rabba said to you: Rabbi Shimon said [this] only with regard to those placed above that one placed below, etc." - It is puzzling: Why did he leave aside [the case of an offering] slaughtered at night, whose blood was spilled, or whose blood went out [of the courtyard], about which Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon disagree, and instead mention those placed above that one placed below, where even Rabbi Yehuda agrees that they do not descend? And Rabbeinu Yitzchak explained that here [the Gemara] is speaking about a bird, whose burnt offering [is supposed to be done] above, and one did it below; and here Rabbi Yehuda does not agree, because it is like a disqualification; therefore they descend. For it is not similar to those placed above that one placed below, of which it says in Zevachim (84a) that Rabbi Yehuda does not disagree, for there it is speaking of an animal, which had a valid preparation in the slaughter and in the receiving [of the blood]; but with a bird burnt offering whose neck was pinched below, where there was no valid preparation at all, Rabbi Yehuda disagrees, as in the case of one slaughtered at night whose blood was spilled. And on this Rabba distinguishes: Rabbi Shimon said that they do not descend (regarding sacrifices) only because he changed [the procedure] with them only at the altar itself, while their slaughter and receiving [of the blood] were always in the north — that is, its whole commandment and all its matters. But if one slaughtered in the south, Rabbi Shimon agrees that it is like one who strangled it, and it is like [offerings] slaughtered outside, since he changed the place of slaughter; and in one who slaughters outside, everyone agrees that if they went up [on the altar], they descend. However, it is difficult for my teacher, our Rabbi Peretz, from that which Rav Yosef objects below to Rabba, "one from the other" etc. — meaning, we see with regard to *melikah* [pinching a bird's neck] that if one changed [the procedure] and it went up, it does not descend, and the same applies to a change in an animal — and Rabba was refuted. But according to Rabbeinu Yitzchak's explanation, why was he refuted from the change of place of *melikah*? Surely he distinguishes well here between a change in a bird and [a change in] the body of the altar, [as in the case of] an animal from north to south! Therefore it seems to me, as is implied by the simple reading, that [the Gemara] is speaking about an animal, and although Rabbi Yehuda agrees about it, nevertheless he brings it as similar to a change of place, as it is like the change of the south, and he mentioned it merely as a mnemonic; but all this is forced. Therefore it appears to my teacher, our Rabbi Peretz, that Rabba needed to bring this matter of those placed above that one placed below, because if he had brought only [the case of] one slaughtered at night, one could certainly distinguish well in that [case], for there it is a change of time and here a change of place, and they are not similar to each other at all. But it would still have been difficult for Rabba from those placed above that one placed below. And if you say: What connection is there between a change in the throwing [of the blood] and a change in slaughter, as with the south? For in this case of those placed above that one placed below, even Rabbi Yehuda agrees, because it is a disqualification in the throwing, whereas here, with the south, it is a disqualification in the slaughter. This is nothing, for according to Rabbi Shimon a disqualification in slaughter is effective just as a disqualification in the throwing is according to Rabbi Yehuda, for in the case of one slaughtered at night, about which Rabbi Yehuda said they descend, Rabbi Shimon said they do not descend; and if so, from now on we should compare one who slaughtered in the south, according to Rabbi Shimon, to those placed above that one placed below, and if so it would be difficult for Rabba. Therefore he needed to distinguish between those placed above and those placed below, [and] between one who slaughtered in the south; but between one slaughtered at night and one who slaughtered in the south he did not need to distinguish, for that distinction is simple and known to all: there it is a change of time and here a change of place:

Tosafot on Meilah 2b:5:1.hebrew: אלא לרבה קשיא - דאמר כמאן דחנקיה דמי, וא"כ הוה ליה כי קדשים שמתו:
Tosafot on Meilah 2b:5:1.english: But according to Rabbah it is difficult - For he said [that the offering] is considered as though [the slaughterer] had strangled it, and if so it is like sacrificial animals that died:

Tosafot on Meilah 2b:6:1.hebrew: ומאי איכא בין דאורייתא לדרבנן - הוה מצי למימר דמדרבנן לא מייתי אשם מעילה, ועדיפא מיניה קא משני: דאפילו חומש ליכא, וכ"ש [דלא מייתי] אשם, דהוה חולין בעזרה:
Tosafot on Meilah 2b:6:1.english: "And what difference is there between [misuse] by Torah law and by rabbinic law?" - [The Gemara] could have said that by rabbinic law one does not bring a guilt offering for misuse, but it answers with something better than that: that there is not even [payment of] the additional one-fifth, and certainly [one does not bring] a guilt offering, since it would be a non-sacred animal [brought] in the Temple courtyard:

Tosafot on Meilah 2b:7:1.hebrew: ומי איכא מעילה מדרבנן - תימה: מאי קא מתמה? אין, איכא טובא! כגון גבי דם, דתנן לקמן (מעילה דף יא.): יצא לנחל קדרון מועלין בו כו', ורוצה לומר מדרבנן. וכן גבי אפר חטאת (בריש) [בסוף] התכלת (מנחות דף נב.). וי"ל דשאני התם דלא בדילי מינייהו, הילכך יש להן לתקן מעילה; אבל הכא גבי קדשים ששחטן בדרום בדילי מינייהו, ועל זה מתמה: איכא מעילה בכה"ג? ומשני: אין, כדאמר עולא, ואף בקדשים שמתו דבדילי יש מעילה מדרבנן:
Tosafot on Meilah 2b:7:1.english: "And is there misuse by rabbinic law?" - This is puzzling: What is [the Gemara] asking? Yes, there is [such a thing] in many cases! For example, regarding blood, as we learned below (Meilah 11a): "If it went out to the Kidron stream, one is liable for misuse of it," etc., which means by rabbinic law. And so too regarding the ashes of a sin offering, at the end of [the chapter] HaTekhelet (Menachot 52a). And one can answer that there it is different, because [the items] have not become separated from [their sacred status]; therefore [the Rabbis] were able to enact [the law of] misuse. But here, regarding sacrificial animals that one slaughtered in the south, they have become separated from [their sacred status], and about this [the Gemara] asks: Is there misuse in such a case? And [the Gemara] answers: Yes, as Ulla said, that even in the case of sacrificial animals that died, which have become separated, there is misuse by rabbinic law:
